subject: info-ds
title: INFO.DS.-----C.CONT.
description: Second diagram on page 289, sitting between the closing fragment of CMOA(II)-47 and the start of CMOA(II)-48 (the 'adaptation cycle of creative music'). Where the first diagram on this page sets up the inversion the principle-exposure cycle produces, this one diagrams the next sequence: INFO-DS (information dissemination — how a thrust alignment actually spreads) crossed with C-CONT (composite continuance — whether the form persists through that spread). (C)INFO-DS is subject in the upper-left with the subject-arrow; C-CONT is the partner-center beside it. From C-CONT, MT-INFO (meta-information) rises up-right and feeds INFO-INTR (information introduction) at the upper right margin, with TRS (transformation) anchoring the right side. PROJ-DY (projection dynamics) sits centrally below C-CONT and drops to CRTF-D (creative-dynamic), which fans into ALT-F (alternative form) on the lower-left of the partner side and SOC-RT-DY (social-reality dynamics) on the lower-right. On the subject side, GRAD (gradualism) descends from INFO-DS to SOC-RT (social reality) at lower-left and to T-C-IMP (temporal-continuity implication) at bottom-center. The structural argument the prose on the facing page makes (CMOA(II)-48): dissemination produces composite-continuance only when each of the cycle's stages — exposure, imitation, stylism, restructuralism — is allowed to actually run. The diagram shows why: the diagonal that pulls MT-INFO down through the partner-side into T-C-IMP (the X-cross with GRAD rising back up) is exactly the temporal mechanism that converts dissemination into continuance. Without that diagonal — without gradualism meeting meta-information on the partner-axis — projection-dynamics produces only creative-dynamic outputs (alt-f, soc-rt-dy) that do not feed back into the subject's continuance chain, and the form arrives without continuing.
